rows.grounds: manner adverb indicating continuation of prescribed procedure
compound expressing a time threshold after three hundred units; internal sandhi within fused form
prescriptive ritual action of offering satisfaction
ritual substance used for the act of satisfaction

items.question: By what means must the deity be satisfied after more than three hundred days?
premises: A prescribed period extends beyond three hundred days.
The deity is the recipient of ritual satisfaction.
Waters serve as the means of performing this satisfaction.
items.inference: Therefore, after more than three hundred days, one should satisfy the deity with waters.
uncertainties: The exact unit counted as three hundred (days or another measure) is not specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Thus, after more than three hundred, one should satisfy the deity with waters.
